name: termeleon
description: Use your existing terminal emulator's color schemes in the integrated terminal.

commands.title: Import Terminal Theme to User Settings…
Import Terminal Theme to Workspace Settings…

termeleon.target.markdownDescription: Which settings file to use for the imported palette. `ask` prompts each time; with no folder open it always uses user settings.

termeleon.livePreview.description: Apply each theme as you navigate through the list. Turn off if the settings.json churn is disruptive.

termeleon.extraDirectories.description: Additional directories to sweep for theme files, e.g. a dotfiles checkout.

termeleon.sources.description: Emulators to scan. Empty means all of them.

configuration.title: Color Preferences when Applying New Themes

termeleon.scopeToActiveTheme.markdownDescription:
VS Code themes may specify terminal colors - most do. When you switch VS Code themes, the terminal colors will normally be replaced. If you've used Termeleon to import terminal colors, what should be done in that situation?

**On:** Imported terminal colors are attached to the VS Code theme that is active at the time of import. When you switch themes, the new theme's terminal colors will be used.

**Off:** Imported terminal colors stay when you switch VS Code themes - even if a VS Code theme provides its own terminal colors.

termeleon.setMinimumContrastRatio.markdownDescription:
VS Code adjusts foreground colors towards a specific contrast target for ease of visibility. Depending on the theme, this can significantly change its appearance.

**On:** Set `#terminal.integrated.minimumContrastRatio#` to 1 to preserve source themes exactly.

**Off:** Allow VS Code to adjust theme display colors..

termeleon.overrideMissingSelectionHighli.markdownDescription:
Some themes do not specify colors for highlighting selected text. In those cases, it can be quite hard to see which text is selected. What should be done in that case?

**On:** invent a highlight color based on the theme's other colors.

**Off:** do not invent one - leave selection colors alone.

termeleon.overrideIncludedSelectionForeg.markdownDescription:
Some themes specify a single foreground color for highlighting selected text. In this case, terminal colors will not be visible in text selections. What should be done in that case?

**On:** ignore the theme's selection foreground and keep each cell's ANSI color.

**Off:** use the theme's selection foreground.
